A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AnyEdit research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–C are readable and matchable, including the image-based dataset examples. No material gap prevents comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original knowledge-editing experiments on two LLMs, including benchmark scores, editing times, chunk-size analysis and generated-output case studies in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendix C, including benchmark comparisons, timing measurements and case studies.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 retains the same chunking, token/layer localization, hidden-state optimization and parameter-update procedure. AnyEdit* and its full-layer updates are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate UnKEBench, AKEW Counterfact/MQUAKE and EditEverything, retaining the same mathematics, code, chemistry, news and poetry coverage. Original, paraphrased and sub-question evaluations remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same pre-edited model and FT-L, MEND, ROME, MEMIT, AlphaEdit and UnKE comparisons. The integrated-method comparisons also match. RLedit is newly cited in related work but is not added to an evaluated comparison.

E3.justification: The two LLMs, batch size of 1, decoding temperature of 0.001, evaluation metrics, sampling procedures and Appendix A.4 optimization settings remain unchanged. Removing the hardware disclosure does not establish a change in the experimental platform.

E4.justification: The format/length diagnostics, integration analysis, chunk-size sensitivity analysis and both Appendix C.1 case studies are retained with the same evidence. Moving the case-study introduction does not add an analysis.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains identical uncertainty entries, Figure 3 retains variance shading, and Figure 5 retains its error bars. No repeated-run counts, seed information or statistical-testing procedures are added or removed.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4, the plotted results and Appendix C.1 outputs match across versions. For example, AnyEdit's original-question BERT Score on Llama3-8B-Instruct/UnKEBench remains 97.76 ± 0.11 in Table 1. Timing values and chunk-size trends are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Proposition 1, the mutual-information formulation and the proofs in Appendices B.2–B.3 retain the same mathematics and assumptions. V3 adds a sentence explaining eta after Equation 4, without revising its definition or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the efficacy-barrier claim, autoregressive editing contribution, mutual-information justification, plug-and-play applicability and claimed 21.5% improvement. Local wording changes do not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: The probability-based explanation of editing limitations and interpretations of generalization, runtime and chunk-size tradeoffs remain unchanged. Section 7 retains the same limitations concerning lifelong editing and multimodal knowledge.

D1.justification: V3 removes Appendix A.4's statement that all experiments used a single A100 GPU with 80 GB memory. Its new acknowledgment names USTC computing resources without equivalent hardware details. Hyperparameters remain unchanged, and the same code URL moves into the abstract.

R1.justification: Section 6 replaces KE with RLedit in its meta-learning examples. Appendix B.1 adds a motivation sentence citing FlipAttack and Structure-guided Large Language Models for Text-to-SQL Generation. These are limited additions; publication updates for retained works such as UnKE and AlphaEdit do not introduce new research comparisons.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized introduction edits, shortens Section 3 headings, explains eta, updates author and correspondence information, and adds acknowledgments and publication details. The overall narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figures 2–3 move from PDF page 3 to 4, and Table 2 moves from page 7 to 8. Some captions are shortened, and appendix spacing and page breaks change. Figure images, table structures and displayed evidence are retained.

improvement.justification: The scientific content and evidence remain unchanged. V3 provides small editorial clarifications and reference updates, but removes the specific hardware disclosure while retaining Table 2's timing claims. The generic computing-resource acknowledgment does not replace that information. This creates a modest loss in reproducibility and interpretability of computational costs that outweighs the limited editorial gains.
